shared_factor_basis.assumptions: Same anchor, linear layer, input/output coordinates, fixed finite PSD Q, finite input second moment, ordinary effective deltas D_i=s_i B_i A_i.
definitions: R=sum_i r_i; A_stack stacks the A_i vertically and B_cat concatenates B_i horizontally.
z=A_stack x; H=E[z z^T]; F=B_cat^T Q B_cat.
C(c) is block diagonal with blocks c_i s_i I_(r_i). Thus D(c)=B_cat C(c) A_stack.
shared_factor_basis.identity: E[(D(c)x)^T Q D(c)x] = tr(C(c) F C(c) H).
shared_factor_basis.proof: Substitute D(c), then use E[z^T C F C z]=tr(C F C E[zz^T]). The scalar block diagonal C is symmetric; all matrices in the trace are R by R.
shared_factor_basis.streaming: For common nonnegative token weights w_t and positive total weight W, accumulate H=(1/W) sum_t w_t z_t z_t^T. This can be done without storing all activations or forming the input second moment in d_in by d_in coordinates.
shared_factor_basis.cost_scope: Moment storage is O(R^2), plus factors and chosen output-metric representation. Computing z still costs O(d_in R) per dense input and outer-product accumulation O(R^2); forming F can be costly for dense Q. This is useful only when R is suitably small and does not make activation acquisition, model inference or numerical precision free.
shared_factor_basis.gauge: Under block invertible G=diag(G_i), B_cat becomes B_cat G and A_stack becomes G^-1 A_stack. F becomes G^T F G and H becomes G^-1 H G^-T. C commutes with G because each block is a scalar multiple of identity, so the trace is unchanged.
limits: This factorization uses one fixed Q. Token-dependent Q(x) generally requires paired statistics; separate average Q and H do not preserve the exact metric.
Different anchors, token populations, masks or incompatible layer coordinates cannot be pooled as though they were one common moment.

If W=0 the metric is unmeasured, not a zero matrix. If K_ii=0 the corresponding functional cosine is undefined. Floating-point PSD errors require explicit diagnostics, not silent evidence of compatibility.

mean_error_does_not_preserve_every_group.population: x=e_1 with probability 99/100 and x=e_2 with probability 1/100; X=diag(99/100,1/100).
mean_error_does_not_preserve_every_group.weighted_optimum: The rank-one optimum is D=diag(1,0), with weighted squared error 1/100. It has zero error on the common group and squared error one on the rare group.
mean_error_does_not_preserve_every_group.rank_obstruction: Exact preservation of T e_1=e_1 and T e_2=e_2 forces D=I_2, of rank two. No rank-one map can meet both exact layer-response constraints.
mean_error_does_not_preserve_every_group.interpretation: Small optimal average local error can coexist with complete loss of a rare direction. Behavioral skill retention still needs independent groupwise endpoints; a weighted spectral optimum is not a guarantee of acquisition or retention.
